body.p: By the present amendment, the claims have been amended as follows:

Claim 1 has been amended to recite, inter alia, that the computing unit is configured to "receive the instructions and the image of the part from the camera; process the instructions to determine the first hardware component to attach to the part; process the image to determine dimensions and an orientation of the part as the part rests on the conveyor; based on the dimensions and the orientation, determine co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component; and control the robotic arm and the multi-functional robotic head to: place the first hardware component on the part at the first position with the first gripping mechanism; and attach the first hardware component to the part at the first position with the first attachment mechanism".
Claim 16 has been amended to be consistent with amended claim 1.
Support for these amendments can be found throughout the application as filed, specifically at paragraphs [0093]-[0099] of the application as published as well as FIGs. 2-5.
Claims 2 and 5 have been cancelled.
Claims 10, 20, 21 and 23 have been amended to be consistent with amended claims 1 and 16.

The amendments to the claims have been made without prejudice and without acquiescing to any of the Examiner's objections. Applicant reserves the right to pursue any deleted or withdrawn subject matter in a further divisional, continuation or continuation-in-part application. No new matter has been entered by the present amendment and its entry is respectfully requested/The amendments do not contain new matter and their entry is respectfully requested.

The Office Action dated August 9, 2024 has been carefully considered. It is believed that the amendments submitted herewith and the following comments represent a complete response to the Examiner's rejections and place the present application in condition for allowance. Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Claims 16, 20-21 and 23-28 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as having insufficient antecedent basis for the term "the first positioned....".
In response, claim 16 has been amended to provide antecedent basis for each of the terms therein.
Claims 20, 21 and 23-28 remain dependent on claim 16 as amended.

In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that the claims, as amended, are clear and requests that this rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) to be withdrawn and that the claims, as amended, be allowed.

Claims 1-10 and 12 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Chen (U.S. 4,613,942, filed Oct. 22, 1984, hereinafter "Chen") in view of Heping (U.S. Pub. No. 2011/0087360, hereinafter "Heping") further in view of Shinozaki (U.S. 9,649,790, hereinafter "Shinozaki") further in view of Ross (NPL- IkeaBot: An Autonomous Multi-Robot Coordinated Furniture Assembly System, published May 2013, pgs. 855-862, hereinafter "Ross").
Claims 16, 20-21 and 23-28 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Chen in view of Heping and further in view of Ross.
Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Notwithstanding this, in an effort to advance prosecution, and without prejudice, claim 1 has been amended to recite, inter alia, that the computing unit is configured to "receive the instructions and the image of the part from the camera; process the instructions to determine the first hardware component to attach to the part; process the image to determine dimensions and an orientation of the part as the part rests on the conveyor; based on the dimensions and the orientation, determine co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component; and control the robotic arm and the multi-functional robotic head to: place the first hardware component on the part at the first position with the first gripping
mechanism; and attach the first hardware component to the part at the first position with the first attachment mechanism".

The amendments to claim 1 clarify that the computing unit received the following information i from the camera of the robotic head: instructions identifying which hardware component(s) to attach to the part (from the scan of the barcode), dimensions of the part (from the image of the part) and an orientation of the part on the conveyor (from the image of the part).

Based on the dimensions of the part and the orientation of the part on the conveyor, the computing unit determines co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component.

Applicant submits that none of the prior art references teaches or suggests receiving dimensions of the part and the orientation of the part from an image of a part, receiving instructions regarding a first hardware component from a barcode on the part and determining, based on the dimensions of the part and the orientation of the part, co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component as claimed in amended claim 1.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for noting, at page 5 of the Office Action, that "Nowhere does Chen teach that the camera is mounted or positioned on a periphery of the robotic head and captures image of the part presented to the robot, instead only barcode image appears to be captured by a stationary camera".

Applicant submits that there is no need for the camera of Chen to be mounted to the robotic head because there is no need for a camera to capture an image of the parts presented to the robotic head in Chen. Rather, in Chen, all of the parts of a same type that are presented to the robot have same dimensions and the orientation of each of the parts is determined by the robot based on the orientation of the indicia on the part. Because the camera in Chen is at a fixed position, the orientation of the part on the conveyor can be determined by comparing the orientation of the indicia of the part to the fixed position of the camera.

Turning to Heping, Heping teaches that does not teach that its processor camera captures an image of the part that is used to determine dimensions of the part. Rather, Heping teaches a camera to image a wheel to determine an orientation pattern of the bolts or studs on the hub.

Applicant submits that none of Chen or Heping teaches or suggests and determining, based on the dimensions of the part and the orientation of the part, co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component as claimed in amended claim 1.

In the present application, a mixture of parts are presented to the robot and the robot first identifies the part, then determines it's dimensions and orientation on the conveyor, then determines what hardware components are to be attached to the part and, finally, determines co-ordinates on the part of a location to attach the hardware component.
The prior art is not concerned with attaching components to the parts that are presented to the robot and, therefore, does not determine co-ordinates of a first location on the part.

Shinozaki and Ross fail to correct the deficiencies of Chen and Heping as each reference also fails to teach or suggest at least "determining, based on the dimensions of the part and the orientation of the part, co-ordinates of a first position on the part to provide the first hardware component" as claimed in amended claim 1.
Therefore, claim 1 as amended is also novel and inventive over Chen, Heping, Shinozaki and Ross, either alone or in any combination.
Applicant submits that claims 3, 4, 6-10 and 12 are therefore also novel and inventive over Chen in view of Shinozaki and further in view of Ross by way of their dependency on claim 1 as amended.

With respect to claims 16, 20-21 and 23-28, Applicant submits that claim 16 as amended corresponds with claim 1 as amended and therefore is novel and inventive over Chen, Heping, Shinozaki and Ross, either alone or in any combination, for at least the same reasons as provided above in support of claim 1 as amended.
Claims 20-21 and 23-28 are therefore also novel and inventive over Chen in view of Shinozaki and further in view of Ross by way of their dependency on claim 16 as amended.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that the claims, as amended, are non- obvious, and requests for this rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 to be withdrawn and that the claims, as amended, be allowed.
